title: Means as sure as the end: elect dying in impenitent vice are not saved
source_text: XVI. Atque huic Thesi haec subditur explicatio: Ex electionis decreto ita ad finem praedestinantur fideles, ut non aliter quam per media a Deo instituta, quasi per viam quandam regiam, ad eundem finem perducantur. Nec minus rata & certa sunt haec Dei decreta de mediis, de modo, ac ordine eventorum, quam de fine ac ipsius eventu. Si quis igitur insistat viam divinae ordinationi contrariam, scilicet latam illam viam immunditiae & impoenitentiae, quae recta ducit ad gehennam, nunquam poterit in coelum ista calleo pervenire. Imo si mors illum oppresserit in hac via errantem, non poterit non ad tartara descendere. Neque fornicarii, neque adulteri, &c. regni Dei haereditatem possidebunt. Frustra ergo sperant qui opinantur electum in talibus flagitiis se volutantem, & ita morientem, vi electionis nihilominus necessario salvandum esse. Nec enim sine poenitentia, & sanctitate nemo videbit Dominum. Sicut ergo certum fuit ex Dei decreto & promissione, illos omnes, qui in eadem cum Paulo navi navigabant, incolumes e naufragio emersuros; & tamen illud Pauli dictum simul certum fuit, Nisi hi manserint in navi, salvi esse non potestis: ita certum fuit, electos Dei servos, Davidem, & Petrum ad regnum coelorum perventuros: & tamen non minus certum, si ille in adulterio & homicidio, hic in abnegatione & perjurio impoenitentes permansissent, quod neuter eorum salvus esse potuisset. Luc. 13. 1 Cor. 6. 9. Heb. 12. 14. Act. 27. 31.
pass_a_gloss: And to this Thesis this explanation is added: By the decree of election the faithful are so predestined to the end that they are brought to the same end not otherwise than through means instituted by God, as through a kind of royal road. Nor are these decrees of God concerning the means, the manner, and the order of events less fixed and certain than those concerning the end and the event itself. If therefore anyone presses a way contrary to the divine ordination—namely that broad way of uncleanness and impenitence which leads straight to Gehenna—he will never be able to arrive in heaven by that path. Nay if death has overtaken him erring in this way, he cannot but descend to Tartarus. Neither fornicators nor adulterers, etc., shall possess the inheritance of the kingdom of God. In vain therefore do they hope who think that an elect person wallowing in such outrages and so dying is nevertheless necessarily to be saved by force of election. For neither without repentance, and without holiness shall anyone see the Lord. As therefore it was certain from God’s decree and promise that all those who were sailing in the same ship with Paul would come safe out of the shipwreck; and yet that saying of Paul was at the same time certain, Unless these abide in the ship, you cannot be saved: so it was certain that God’s elect servants, David and Peter, would come to the kingdom of heaven; and yet no less certain that if the one had remained impenitent in adultery and homicide, the other in denial and perjury, neither of them could have been saved. Luke 13. 1 Cor. 6:9. Heb. 12:14. Acts 27:31.
pass_b_english: Election’s end travels a fixed road of means; the broad path of impenitent vice never reaches heaven.
Paul’s shipwreck word and David/Peter show: elect dying unrepentant in grave sin would not be saved.

choices.why: Appointed path of means to the end.
